etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English joyous, joious, from Old French joieus, from joie + -eus.

quote.citation: 1998 November 30, Björk (lyrics and music), “Alarm Call”, in Homogenic, One Little Indian Records, →OCLC:
quote.text: I want to go on a mountain top / With a radio and good batteries / To play a joyous tune and / Free the human race / From suffering

quote.citation: 2018 July 7, Phil McNulty, “Sweden 0-2 England”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Southgate and his England players repeated the scenes from the dramatic penalty shootout win over Colombia as they celebrated in front of joyous supporters at the final whistle – one step closer to history and with expectation levels raised once more as they stand one game away from football's greatest occasion.
